For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the infant Food Puree Fruit came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-infant-food-puree-fruit" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-infant-food-puree-fruit-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of infant food puree fruit, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed infant Food Puree Fruit in the same study and group. Infant Food Puree Fruit, juice (Fruits) had lead higher at 2.3 µg/kg, against 0.9 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (infant food puree fruit, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Analytical Results for Lead in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2020-FY2021)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-infant-food-puree-fruit-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-infant-food-puree-fruit-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of infant Food Puree Fruit measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of infant Food Puree Fruit measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 19 groups of infant Food Puree Fruit ranged from 1,440 µg/kg (outbreak product) to 6,430 µg/kg (outbreak product); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cataldo2026-apple-cinnamon-puree-lead-chromate|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cataldo N, Weed BD, Lewis K, Kirchner M, Arnold K, Michael L, Chang A, Daniel JH, Shone S, Yeung L, Mangia J, Troeschel A, Morales J, Kubachka KM, Witkowski M, Schaufler L, Abt E, Pauley S, Ruckart P, Yeh M, Williams TL, Gray P, Hurt D, Salter M, Howard M, Harris S · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cataldo2026-apple-cinnamon-puree-lead-chromate">International Investigation of Lead and Chromium Contamination in Imported Apple Puree</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Health 89(1):20-27</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cataldo2026-apple-cinnamon-puree-lead-chromate">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, total arsenic across 26 groups of infant Food Puree Fruit ranged from 0.32 µg/kg (puree product 40 (manufacturer category G)) to 20.2 µg/kg (puree product 12 (manufacturer category E)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Brian P. Jackson, Vivien F. Taylor, Tracy Punshon, Kathryn L. Cottingham · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Arsenic concentration and speciation in infant formulas and first foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pure and Applied Chemistry, Vol. 84, No. 2, pp. 215-223</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-infant-food-puree-fruit" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-infant-food-puree-fruit" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in infant Food Puree Fruit?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in infant Food Puree Fruit?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same infant Food Puree Fruit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Analytical Results for Lead in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2020-FY2021)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Infant Food Puree Fruit, juice (Fruits) had lead higher at 2.3 µg/kg, against 0.9 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (infant food puree fruit, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Analytical Results for Lead in Food Intended for Babies and Young Children (FY2020-FY2021)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2021-lead-baby-food-fy2020-fy2021">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-infant-food-puree-fruit-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-infant-food-puree-fruit-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in infant Food Puree Fruit is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in infant Food Puree Fruit is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in infant Food Puree Fruit, as sold from 2 results in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 20 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
